W5 (contrarian), after E012.
1. Accuracy comes mostly from the optimizer and averaging. Lookahead added about +1.0 pp (E005). Muon added +0.66 pp at batch 2000 (E006). Muon's update has no weight-decay term and it renormalizes each filter to norm sqrt(out_channels) every step, so WD reaches only BN biases, the whitening bias and the head. That makes WD-grid ideas (I019) close to no-ops: they amount to a reshuffle plus a small head/bias effect. Decaying LR to 0 hurt by 0.26 pp (E009), which fits Lookahead already supplying the late-phase noise reduction. The two are redundant, or LR=0 over-damps them.
2. Lookahead is not just endpoint averaging. Resetting the fast weights every 5 steps damps Muon's large fixed-norm steps. With the alpha ramp ((t/T)^3), the averaging horizon is only about 20 steps at the end. My guess is that the trajectory effect matters, so a plain EMA (I022) loses a little.
3. Time is GPU compute, scaling with pixels times width. Gentle resizing was free (E007, -20%). Resizing to 20 px fell off a cliff (E011, -1.4 pp), probably from scale mismatch and too few steps at 32 px. Cutting width from 576 to 512 saved 9.4%, more than its FLOP share (tile alignment). It cost 0.43 pp versus E007, more than the 0.3 pp H1.5.2 allowed.
4. The step is about 28 ms at batch 2000, about 237 steps (HYP epochs=9.5, not 9). Per step the CPU issues compiled fwd/bwd, compiled Muon, fused SGD and foreach Lookahead, with no per-step host sync. The only syncs are the 25 boolean-mask indexings per epoch in augment. So the run is mostly GPU-bound, and CUDA graphs or break removal can buy only about 2-4%. The sync bubbles at epoch boundaries are the real, small target.
5. Noise: E012 reproduced E010's accuracy bit-for-bit and its time within 0.1%. Compiled runs are deterministic per seed, and time noise is about ±1-2%. Any change that alters RNG consumption or kernel choice (autotune, a fused augment) reshuffles the 3-seed mean by up to ±0.3 pp. With 0.18 pp margin, roughly 30-40% of "neutral" changes would fall below 0.753 from reshuffle alone. The feasibility verdict is dominated by that, not by the mechanism.
6. A mechanism nobody has proposed: the late 32 px phase (the last 30% of steps) is where accuracy is set. The cheapest accuracy may come from moving the 28→32 switch earlier, or from using a 2nd resolution of 30 px, rather than from optimizer knobs. Max-pool heads are scale-sensitive at test time.
Unsure about: E012's held-out seed mean (not shown) and whether seeds 0-2 are lucky; Muon lr sensitivity on CIFAR-100; the cost of prepare (H2D copy of 150 MB unpinned plus eigh plus pad, guessed at 0.15-0.3 s).

forecasts.reason: GPU-bound at about 28 ms per step with no per-step syncs, so graphs give about 2-3%; max-autotune kernel changes may reshuffle accuracy.
0.24 was tuned for this fixed-norm parametrization; 1.5x is likely neutral or slightly worse, and a +0.3 pp gain is unlikely.
WD never reaches the Muon filters (they are renormalized each step), so only the head and BN biases change; the result is a reshuffle-sized effect.
Few breaks or syncs beyond augment's mask indexing; saves under 3%, and folding augment changes RNG so accuracy is not bit-identical.
Lookahead's reset damps Muon's trajectory; a plain EMA with a ~20-step horizon probably loses 0.2-0.4 pp, straddling the 0.3 pp threshold.

cruxes: E012 held-out seeds 3-12: is the 10-seed mean above or below 0.753? If seeds 0-2 are lucky, the tip is not truly feasible and every time cut needs an accuracy buy-back first.
What fraction of the 6.64 s is GPU idle (profiler)? If it is under 5%, CUDA graphs and break removal are dead ends, and only pixels, width and epochs move time.

Does accuracy depend mainly on the steps spent at 32 px (late phase)? If so, reshaping the resize schedule (e.g. 24→32 with an earlier switch, or a 30 px middle stage) beats optimizer tuning for buying margin.
